operational_privacy.attestation_meaning: Operator declaration only; it is not proof of account state.
operational_privacy.required_account_evidence: A redacted receipt proving Input & Output Logging is disabled globally or the dedicated Friendly Bot API key is explicitly excluded.

decoded_response_lifecycle.client_contract: GatewayHttpClient.post receives an operation decoder and returns only a validated configured key, nonempty persona summary, validated local alias, or typed static protocol/transport failure; it returns no raw response object to a public gateway operation.
decoded_response_lifecycle.non_2xx: HTTPError and other non-2xx outcomes are status-only transport failures; their provider bodies are never read.
decoded_response_lifecycle.success: A 2xx stdlib body is read at most limit plus one bytes, rejected if oversize, parsed and operation-validated in the same low-level scope, and the local bytearray is cleared before the safe outcome returns.
decoded_response_lifecycle.ordinary_failures: IncompleteRead, malformed/deep JSON, decoder failures, and discard/close failures become static protocol or retryable transport outcomes after the raw scope exits; BaseException and cancellation are not caught.
decoded_response_lifecycle.outbound_cleanup: The caller-owned headers and payload are cleared before the final safe outcome; a stdlib worker receives an isolated snapshot and clears it after its own lifecycle so cancellation does not dispatch an empty payload.
decoded_response_lifecycle.public_error_boundary: GatewayError is constructed only after the lifecycle returns a safe outcome. Its message, args, cause, context, and attributes contain only static safe summaries; the gateway does not log these errors.
decoded_response_lifecycle.scope_limit: This is not a universal assertion that arbitrary live Python frame inspection cannot find transient self, request, prompt, or credential references during normal execution. It guarantees the normal returned-response and raised-gateway-error boundary for raw provider response bytes.
